Aisha: Quick heads-up — in the v2.1 quant bring-up I noticed NDCG@10 drop on short queries when we prime with wildcard tokens (`*` / `<WILDCARD>`). Anyone else hitting this?
Ben: Yep, same here. Short queries (<=5 tokens) MRR ~ -3.1%, NDCG@10 ~ -2.8% vs baseline. Repro'd on one holdout shard.
Maria: Can you share the eval command you ran?
Ben: `./eval/rerank --model v2.1-q8 --cohort=short_queries --priming=wildcard --k=10 --tokenize=bytepair`
Aisha: Output excerpt:
```
k=10: NDCG@10 0.742 -> 0.721
MRR  0.419 -> 0.406
slice: short_queries
```
Ciara: Interesting. Could this be a tokenizer/subtoken alignment issue? Wildcards produce extra subtoken boundary and that shifts attention positions.
Maria: Also check holdout sampling — if short queries are oversampled in the cohort it can exaggerate the effect.
Ben: I switched priming to explicit example prompt (no wildcard) and delta vanished.
Aisha: Hypothesis: wildcard primes create inconsistent prefix cache keys, changing KV packing behavior during decoding -> small scoring drift that matters for top ranks.
Ciara: Quick repro plan:
- run eval with `--tokenize=normalize` and `--no-kv-caching`
- run with holdout_by_user vs random
- add synthetic short-query priming ablation (replace `*` with random token)
Aisha: I've kicked off eval-bot: `rerank-eval/1762504321/priming-ablate` — will post results
eval-bot: job started: rerank-eval/1762504321/priming-ablate (link: https://ci.internal/reports/1762504321)
Ben: I'll try the `--no-kv-caching` run now and post logs
Maria: If kv-caching is the culprit we should add a short-query regression test to the smoke suite.
Aisha: Agreed — assigning follow-up: create a small golden set of 500 short queries and add ablation to ci/smoke. @Ben can you open the PR?
Ben: Yep, will open PR and link results.
Ciara: Thanks — this one felt subtle but actionable. :thumbsup:
